FITTING
19.1 INTRODUCTION
The garment which fits well on body looks good. Often, when one does not have adequate
knowledge of the garments made, do not fit well. Hence, it is essential for a tailor to know
the reasons for the ill fit of any garment made. These reasons can be kept in mind while
measuring and cutting the cloth so that a good fitting can be achieved. It is necessary to
try on the garment before fmal ~nishing so that any defects in fitting can be taken care of
19.2 OBJECTIVE
After reading this lesson, you will be able to:
•
explain fitting in garments;
•
identify and correct defects in fitting;
•
give a good fitting to garments.
19.3 FITTING
Any garment which sits well on the body is said to have good 'fitting'. In order to get a
good fitting, it is necessary to try on the garment before final fmishing so that any defects
in fitting can be identified and removed. A garment which does not have good fitting does
not look good when worn. Defects in fitting could be because measurements were not
taken properly. When a garment is tried on, these defects can be taken care of and the
resultant garment will be a well fitting one. The garment may get mis-shapen ifit is opened

19.5 REASONS FOR FITTING DEFECTS
As mentioned
above, the defects in fitting should be marked during trial and corrected
later on. But more important
is to know the reasons
for these defects so that in future,
these can be avoided. A tailor learns through experience
what these reasons could be and
the more experienced
a tailor is, the lesser will be fitting defects in the garments he makes.
Fitting defects generally
occur due to the following
reasons-
1.
Poor Cutting
Defects may occur if one has not been cautious during cutting of cloth, ifthe lay
out had not been properly inspected before cutting or if one has not been careful
while cutting curved areas. Experience helps in proper cutting. One has to carefully
inspect the cloth before cutting. In this way majority
of defects can be avoided
by careful cutting.
2.
Poor Stitching
A garment will have a poor fitting ifthe cutting and stitching is defective. Even if
one has cut the cloth properly,
but the garment
is poorly stitched,
it will have
defects in fitting, hence, one must be very careful while working, to avoid defects
in the garment.
-
3.
Wrong marking
Sometimes
it may happen
that markings
are made on the garment
in order to
rectify some defect. But in the process of trying to correct one defect, some other
defect arises. This may happen because the marking placed for defect correction
may be wrongly marked.
4.
Cutting with wrong layout
Ifthe layout on the cloth is not correct and the cloth is cut without allowances
for
seams and turnings,
the garment
is bound to be defective.

5.
Customers preferences
Sometimes, even if the garment is well made, it may not be to the personal liking
of a customer. Every person has preferences and these must be clearly asked for
before stitching so that later on, the garment fits the person to his or her liking.
6.
Fabric
The choice of fabric sometimes leads to fitting defects. For example, iftwo salwars
are made one of cotton cloth and other with satin, with the same measurements,
the one made of cotton cloth will be well fitting but the one made of satin will be
too long. This is because the weight ofthe satin pulls it down and it appears to
be longer. Hence the tailor should have the knowledge that for such fabrics, the
full length should be kept slightly less so that the final garment gives a good fit.
7.
Inferior trimming
One should always use trimming of good quality. Use of poor quality trimming
may give rise to defects in fitting.
8.
Fussy customer
Some people are extremely fussy about their clothes. Hence, even clothes which
are well made and well fitting may appear ill-fitting to them.
9.
Differences between cutter and tailor
If the cutter and the tailor do not have a mutual understanding of how the other
works, the resultant garment may have some defects.
10.
Poor workmanship
A poor workman end up making a poor garment. Good training and experience
is a must for a good tailor. Only then will they be able to make good garments.
11.
Unshrunk fabric
If the fabric has not been soaked and shrunk before cutting, then after the garment
is ready, and is washed, it will shrink and become smallerin size. This will lead
to poor fitting.
12.
Disregard of allowances for growth
When garments are made for people growing up, proper allowances have to be
kept otherwise the garment soon becomes short/tight.
